To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dominant microstructures in supercritical collisionless perpendicular shocks are: (a) in 2-D the field-parallel propagative fluctuations driven by the Weibel instability and (b) in 3-D the counter-propagating fluctuations driven by the interaction of reflected ions and field-aligned propagative fluctuations in the ramp.

the microstructure of perpendicular shocks is dominated by fluctuations generated at the upstream edge and the foot by the Weibel instability driven by the gyrating ions reflected at the magnetic field ramp, and by fluctuations generated by the coupling of the reflected ions with propagating fluctuations in field-parallel direction.
the microstructure in supercritical perpendicular collisionless shocks is due to the motion of gyrating ions reflected from the shock front, and that this is true in 2-D and 3-D.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the microstructure in collisionless shocks, in particular, with the question of what causes the microstructure.
the structure of collisionless shocks, with a focus on the microstructure.
the study of collisionless shocks in plasmas, in particular with the microstructure of such shocks and the mechanisms responsible for it.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the microstructure in perpendicular shocks is due to a combination, depending on the shock parameters, of Weibel-like instabilities driven by the reflected ions at the shock front and a coupling between reflected-gyrating motion and field-parallel propagations in the shock ramp.
the microstructure of supercritical perpendicular shocks is due to the motion of the gyrating reflected ions.
microstructure in collisionless perpendicular shocks is generated by the ion Weibel and the reflected-ion instabilities, both of which are driven at the shock upstream edge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dominant microstructures in perpendicular shocks are driven by the reflected ions.
the microstructure is a consequence of the dynamics of the reflected ions in a supercritical shock.
the microstructure in collisionless shocks is due primarily to a combination of the motion of reflected ions and the Weibel instability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microstructure of collisionless shocks is determined by the coupling between the reflected ions and the field-parallel propagations in the shock ramp.

the microstructure of perpendicular shocks in the coplanarity plane is due to the motion of ions specularly reflecting at the magnetic ramp and that the Weibel instability, while present, is not the dominant source of microstructure in this plane.

, while the macrostructure of perpendicular collisionless supercritical shocks is primarily determined by the dynamics of reflected ions, the microstructure is due mainly to the Weibel instability driven by the reflected ions at the upstream edge and the reflected-gyrated ions in the ramp.
